ai.description: This slender snake reaches 40–50 cm. It is dark brown with a distinct pale vertebral stripe and a narrow, pointed head. The scales are smooth, and the snout is notably wedge-shaped.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Xylophis perroteti* is best distinguished by its lack of a loreal scale and the presence of a distinct, dark mid-dorsal stripe running the length of its iridescent body.
ai.habitat: *Xylophis perroteti* inhabits high-altitude montane shola forests and adjacent grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Striped Narrow-headed Snake is primarily diurnal and specializes in foraging for earthworms within the leaf litter and soft soil of high-altitude mountain forests.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Xylophis perroteti* is oviparous, laying a small clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly after.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Xylophis perroteti* is endemic to the high-elevation shola forests and grasslands of the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, India.
